Yes. The subtext enriches the story naturally rather than feeling forced. Marian’s candlelit visit to Anton’s doorway—“I have a torch” / “I know”—suggests an invitation neither will acknowledge directly. Their carefully maintained gentleness, his briefly lingering hands, and her request that he say her name again convey attraction constrained by his marriage and their impending separation.

The coastal setting deepens this emotional tension: the rising tide makes their temporary refuge inaccessible, while its eventual erasure echoes the approaching end of their time together. These meanings emerge through concrete actions and restrained dialogue rather than imposed explanations.
